newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down, sentiment bearish.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down, sentiment bearish.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended on a bearish note on Friday as the market drifted skittishly below New York's Thursday close, following a physical buying spree in early trade, gold dealers and traders said.
Bullion ended at US$377.60/378.10 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$377.90/378.40 close on Thursday.
"We saw good physical offtake from our customers this morning," said the chief bullion trader at a local bank.
Physical buying below US$377.50 per ounce led to a slight rebound in the gold prices later in the day, with gold edging up to $377.70/378.20 per ounce in mid-afternoon.
Physical buying was countered by producer selling, mostly from Australia, dealers said.
With market direction still uncertain after constant two-way business, some players felt further buying could be risky, specially if gold fell below $377 per ounce, gold dealers said.
"After $377 per ounce, $372 is what people are watching," said a gold dealer at another local bullion firm, adding that market sentiment remained very bearish.
Liquidity was tight, as many traders were heavily short in anticipation of further price drops, one senior gold dealer at an international bullion firm said.
"People are dreaming of $372.00 per ounce," the trader said.
Gold traders also noted that gold interest rates had edged up further, making it more expensive to borrow the yellow metal.
Gold lease rates climbed from over 2.10 percent for one month on Tuesday and Wednesday to about 2.90 on Friday for one month, on the Reuters' GOFO page (showing gold lending rates).
Local gold ended HK$15 lower at HK$3,481 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -6.00.
